summary: Alan Watts was a scholar in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Bexley Seabury Seminary and under teachers including D. T. Suzuki and Sokei-an. His career included posts at Northwestern University, the American Academy of Asian Studies, and Esalen Institute.

Alasdair MacIntyre was a philosopher who studied at Queen Mary University of London and the University of Manchester. He held academic posts at Essex, Brandeis, Duke, the University of Notre Dame, and London Metropolitan University.

Alasdair Urquhart is a philosopher who completed his MA at the University of Edinburgh and his PhD at the University of Pittsburgh. He held posts at the University of Toronto Mississauga and the University of Toronto.

Alastair Gornall works in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning his PhD from the University of Cambridge. He has held positions at SOAS University of London, the Singapore University of Technology and Design, and the Pali Text Society.
Albert Debrunner was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Jacob Wackernagel, among others. He held academic posts at the universities of Zurich, Greifswald, Bern, Jena, and Basel.

Albert Grünwedel worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After earning his Dr. phil. from the University of Munich, he served as a director at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin and held an honorary professorship at Humboldt University.

Albert Hoefer was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Greifswald, Göttingen, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as a professor at the University of Greifswald from circa 1840 to 1883 and founded the Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache.
Albert Hofmann studied at the University of Zurich from 1925 to 1929. He subsequently held a long-term post at Novartis from around 1929 to 1971.

Albert Lutz is a specialist in Sinology and history and archaeology. After studying at the University of Zurich under Helmut Brinker and Eberhard Fischer, he served as curator of Chinese art and later director at Museum Rietberg.

Albert Schweitzer worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the German University of Prague, the University of Tübingen, and the University of Strasbourg, where he also held a post from around 1902 to 1913.
Albert Sechehaye was a linguist who studied at the University of Geneva from 1889 to 1898 under Ferdinand de Saussure. He subsequently held a post at the University of Geneva from circa 1903 to 1946.

Albert Thumb was a linguist and Indologist who completed his habilitation at the University of Freiburg under Rudolf Thurneysen. He held teaching posts at the University of Freiburg, the University of Marburg, and the University of Strasbourg.

Albert Welter is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara and held faculty posts at the University of Winnipeg and the University of Arizona.
Alberto Todeschini is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He has held positions at the Institute for Research in Humanities at Kyoto University and the Italian School of East Asian Studies.

Albion Moonlight Butters specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard Divinity School, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Columbia University, where he completed his PhD under Robert A. F. Thurman.

Albrecht Hanisch is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn. He has served as Acting Director of the Nepal Research Centre and with the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

Albrecht Weber was an Indologist who studied at Breslau, Bonn, and Berlin under scholars including Christian Lassen and Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. He held long-term posts at Humboldt University of Berlin and was a member of the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

Albrecht Wezler was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Tübingen under Paul Thieme. He served as Director at the University of Hamburg, the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project, and the Nepal Research Centre.

Aleix Ruiz-Falqués specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Eivind Kahrs and has held posts at the Singapore University of Technology and Design and Shan State Buddhist University.

Aleksander Brückner was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Lviv, Vienna, and Frederick William University Berlin, subsequently holding posts at the University of Lviv and Frederick William University Berlin.
